Summoned Companions

You call across a boundary, and something answers: paws on stone, a flicker of ancestral light, a shape unfolding from cold air. The creature acts through your attention. Its presence gives you choices, not a second independent turn.

Choose from the profiles in this chapter when a summoning ability permits the category and tier. Higher-tier cards can choose eligible lower-tier creatures. Category names alone do not grant access to an unlisted creature.

Summons are energy forms shaped to resemble creatures. They cannot receive healing and disappear at 0 HP without leaving a body. They occupy squares, block movement, take damage and can be pushed or grappled normally unless the profile says otherwise; energy form grants no automatic incorporeality or immunity.

Command the creature

Spend your Main Action to give one summon a Main Action and a Maneuver. Spend your Maneuver to give one summon a Maneuver and movement. Normal conversions apply. The Main-command package has no separate movement allowance: convert its Maneuver to movement if it needs to approach before attacking.

A summon receives at most one command on your turn. You can spend your Main Action on one creature and your Maneuver on another. A summoning card's immediate free Main command counts as that creature's command for the turn.

An uncommanded summon does nothing. It does not follow, keep watch, alert you, continue a previous task, or take Reactions and opportunity attacks. Existing conditions, durations and passive defenses still operate. Resolve its turn-based timing on your turn. You cannot summon creatures that summon more creatures.

Keep the connection

A summon disappears beyond 6 squares from you, including after forced movement of either participant. It also disappears at 0 HP, or when you become unconscious or die. Its duration may end earlier. It leaves no permanent equipment or loot.

Measure the tether between the nearest occupied squares of controller and summon, using ordinary grid distance. At 6 squares the summon remains; beyond 6 it immediately disappears. The nearest square of a large form sets the distance.

Healing through a summon

When a summon uses a printed healing ability, you pay its HP cost once before resolution, bypassing resistance. You must remain above 0 HP after payment. The summon uses its own attribute and outcomes and still requires its command and action. It can heal an eligible other creature, but cannot receive healing. Ordinary unsummoned healers pay their own cost.

Give a useful order

“Attack that creature,” “defend this spot,” “move into cover,” and “help them cross” are clear intentions. The creature still needs the printed capability and enough commanded actions to carry them out. A previous order never buys activity next turn. Outside combat, you must continue directing a longer task for its full time.

Roll the creature's attack attribute, not your own, and read its player-facing attacker outcomes. When it is attacked, roll the defense attribute named by the incoming attack using the creature's value. Apply the profile's attack or defense Boons/Banes and resistance normally. There is never a second opposed roll.

The profiles below include only the summoned form's permitted capabilities. A monster's dramatic description does not grant its summoned form extra actions, active auras, independent attacks or skills.
